comparisons.peer_topic: 2024 Process Node Manufacturing Status and Roadmap Changes
comparisons.peer_summary: As of the end of 2024, most products were manufactured using the Intel 7 node, while high-volume production of the Intel 4 and Intel 3 nodes was shifted to Ireland. The company canceled the productization of Intel 20A to focus on the improved Intel 18A node, which is expected to enter high-volume production in 2025.
comparisons.comparison: Both Micron and Intel disclose the volume production status and roadmap progression of their latest semiconductor manufacturing nodes in 2024. Micron reports that its 9th-generation Micron G9 NAND node began volume production in 2024 and is ramping, while Intel reports shifting high-volume production of its Intel 4 and Intel 3 nodes to Ireland in 2024 and canceling the Intel 20A node to focus on the improved Intel 18A node expected in 2025.

sentences.text: In 2024, we began volume production of Micron G9 NAND, representative of the industry's ninth-generation 3D NAND node.
Micron G8 and G9 NAND nodes are ramping in high volume and will become an increasing portion of our mix through 2025.

As of the end of 2024, a significant majority of our products were manufactured using our Intel 7 process node in Arizona and Israel, we successfully ramped our Intel 4 and Intel 3 process nodes as our first EUV lithography nodes and shifted high-volume production of those nodes to Ireland, and we canceled the productization of our Intel 20A process node to focus efforts on the improved version of the node, Intel 18A, that we expect to put into high-volume production in 2025 with our new client family of products code-named Panther Lake.

comparisons.peer_topic: Intel 4 process node production status and capabilities
comparisons.peer_summary: Intel 4, the first EUV lithography node, delivered significant density scaling and approximately 20% performance-per-watt improvement over Intel 7; it moved to high-volume manufacturing in Ireland in 2024 for the Intel Core Ultra processor and is expected to represent an increasing portion of production in 2025.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies describe specific capabilities and high-volume manufacturing status for their respective advanced nodes introduced or ramped in 2024. Micron highlights Micron G9 as the industry's ninth-generation 3D NAND node ramping in high volume, whereas Intel highlights Intel 4 as its first EUV lithography node with significant density scaling and performance-per-watt improvements moving to high-volume manufacturing in Ireland in 2024.
